daily_quests.title: ASX 200 Volatility Rankings with Window Functions
daily_quests.description: Using ASX 200 historical price data, calculate the 30-day rolling standard deviation of daily returns for each stock using window functions. Rank stocks by volatility within each month using ROW_NUMBER(). Then use a CTE to identify the top 5 most volatile stocks each month. Your output should show: stock_code, month, volatility_rank, rolling_std_dev, and average_closing_price for that month. Order by month descending, then rank ascending.

daily_quests.title: NSW Road Crash Data Cleaning & Aggregation Pipeline
daily_quests.description: Download NSW Road Crash Data and build a cleaning script that: (1) removes rows with missing crash_date or location coordinates, (2) standardises speed_zone values to uppercase and handles typos (e.g. '50 km/h', '50kmh', '50KM/H' all become '50'), (3) creates a new column crash_hour extracted from crash_time, (4) filters to crashes from 2020 onwards only, (5) exports a cleaned CSV with columns: crash_id, crash_date, crash_hour, speed_zone, location, severity. Write your script to handle at least 3 common data quality issues and log how many rows were removed at each step.

daily_quests.title: Great Barrier Reef Monitoring: SQL Analysis + Python Reporting
daily_quests.description: Part 1 (SQL): Using Great Barrier Reef monitoring data, write a query that calculates: coral_bleaching_percentage by reef_site and monitoring_year, using LAG() to show year-over-year change in bleaching percentage, and RANK() to identify the top 10 most affected reefs across all years. Part 2 (Python): Import this SQL result into pandas and create a summary report that: (1) identifies reefs with worsening trends (bleaching increased for 3+ consecutive years), (2) calculates the average rate of change in bleaching percentage per reef, (3) exports a markdown report with headers, tables, and key findings. Combine the SQL output and Python analysis into one final CSV showing reef_site, year, bleaching_pct, yoy_change, and trend_direction.
